[heat_action_plan_01] অফিসিয়াল নির্দেশিকা অনুসারে:
## Early Warning System and Temperature Thresholds (Source: DDMA Heat Action Plan, Page 10 & 42)
- District administrations and municipal corporations activate Heat Action Plans based on forecasted temperature thresholds.
- Alert levels: Yellow Watch (Hot day advisory >= 40 °C in plains), Orange Alert (Be Prepared for severe heat stress), and Red Warning (Take Action for extreme heat conditions).
- Inter-agency coordination: Nodal disaster officers coordinate municipal water tankers, public drinking water kiosks (Piyau), and emergency health centres.
- Public awareness campaigns and early warnings disseminated via SMS, mobile apps, local media, and transit announcements 24 to 48 hours in advance.

অফিসিয়াল নির্দেশিকা অনুসারে:
এই বিষয়ে কোনো সরকারি নির্দেশিকা পাওয়া যায়নি। জরুরি সহায়তার জন্য ১১২ (জরুরি সেবা), ১০৭৭ (দুর্যোগ ব্যবস্থাপনা) বা ১৮০০-১৮০-১৫৫১ (কিষাণ কল সেন্টার) নম্বরে যোগাযোগ করুন।

[flood_cyclone_safety_02] অফিসিয়াল নির্দেশিকা অনুসারে:
## Cyclone and Lightning Safety Measures (Source: IMD-NDMA Guidelines, Page 1-3)
- Cyclone precautions: inspect and secure loose roof tiles or tin sheets; board or tape glass windows.
- Keep emergency kits ready: non-perishable food, potable drinking water, torches, battery radio, and first-aid supplies.
- Unhook and disconnect electrical appliances during cyclones to prevent short-circuits and electrical fires.
- Lightning safety 30/30 rule: if the time between lightning flash and thunder is less than 30 seconds, take shelter indoors; wait 30 minutes after last thunder before heading outdoors.
- If outdoor during lightning: avoid tall isolated trees, open fields, elevated ridges, and metal structures; if hair stands on neck, squat low with hands on knees.

[icar_agriculture_advisory_02] অফিসিয়াল নির্দেশিকা অনুসারে:
## Cold Wave, Frost and Ground Freeze Crop Protection (Source: IMD Agrimet Agriculture Guidance, Page 2-3)
- Apply light and frequent irrigation or sprinkler irrigation in evening hours to protect crops from cold injury and ground frost.
- In rice nursery beds: cover nursery beds with polythene sheets during the night and remove in the morning; irrigate in the evening and drain out in the morning.
- Cover young orchard fruit plants with straw, sarkanda, gunny bags, or polythene sheets.
- To protect sensitive crops like mustard, gram, and rajmah from frost injury, spray dilute sulphuric acid @ 0.1% (1 L in 1000 L water) or thiourea @ 500 ppm.
- Animal husbandry in winter: keep cattle and goats inside sheds during night, provide dry bedding, and supplement daily feed with mineral mixtures, salt, and jaggery.

## Extreme Heat and Drought Crop Management (Source: IMD Agrimet Agriculture Guidance, Page 4)
- Apply light and frequent irrigation to standing crops during evening or early morning hours to maintain root zone moisture and reduce soil surface temperature.
- Increase frequency of irrigation during critical crop growth stages (tillering, flowering, grain filling).
- Mulch with crop residue, straw, or polythene sheets to conserve soil moisture and suppress evaporative loss.
- Use sprinkler and drip irrigation systems to optimize water use efficiency under heat stress.
- Protect farm animals and cattle: keep animals under shade, provide ample cool drinking water, cool sheds with straw/dung-mud plaster or water foggers, and graze only during cooler morning and evening hours.

## Extreme Heat and Drought Crop Management (Source: IMD Agrimet Agriculture Guidance, Page 4)
- Apply light and frequent irrigation to standing crops during evening or early morning hours to maintain root zone moisture and reduce soil surface temperature.
- Increase frequency of irrigation during critical crop growth stages (tillering, flowering, grain filling).
- Mulch with crop residue, straw, or polythene sheets to conserve soil moisture and suppress evaporative loss.
- Use sprinkler and drip irrigation systems to optimize water use efficiency under heat stress.
- Protect farm animals and cattle: keep animals under shade, provide ample cool drinking water, cool sheds with straw/dung-mud plaster or water foggers, and graze only during cooler morning and evening hours.

## Extreme Heat and Drought Crop Management (Source: IMD Agrimet Agriculture Guidance, Page 4)
- Apply light and frequent irrigation to standing crops during evening or early morning hours to maintain root zone moisture and reduce soil surface temperature.
- Increase frequency of irrigation during critical crop growth stages (tillering, flowering, grain filling).
- Mulch with crop residue, straw, or polythene sheets to conserve soil moisture and suppress evaporative loss.
- Use sprinkler and drip irrigation systems to optimize water use efficiency under heat stress.
- Protect farm animals and cattle: keep animals under shade, provide ample cool drinking water, cool sheds with straw/dung-mud plaster or water foggers, and graze only during cooler morning and evening hours.

## Extreme Heat and Drought Crop Management (Source: IMD Agrimet Agriculture Guidance, Page 4)
- Apply light and frequent irrigation to standing crops during evening or early morning hours to maintain root zone moisture and reduce soil surface temperature.
- Increase frequency of irrigation during critical crop growth stages (tillering, flowering, grain filling).
- Mulch with crop residue, straw, or polythene sheets to conserve soil moisture and suppress evaporative loss.
- Use sprinkler and drip irrigation systems to optimize water use efficiency under heat stress.
- Protect farm animals and cattle: keep animals under shade, provide ample cool drinking water, cool sheds with straw/dung-mud plaster or water foggers, and graze only during cooler morning and evening hours.
